solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Citizen removing power from Trump perhaps

indicators.note: removing says a letter is taken away from the title Trump held

parts.note: Donald Trump is an example of a president
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A citizen strips authority from a former US leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident is someone who lives in a place, as a citizen of a town does.

clue.text: Secluded spot for a break

definitions.meaning: a nook or alcove set back from the main space
a pause, as in a school playtime or parliamentary holiday

explanation.surface: Somewhere quiet to go during a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an alcove or hidden corner; the other is an interval or holiday.

clue.text: The king governs English island badly

indicators.note: badly says the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that the monarch runs an English island poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign is a supreme ruler, such as a reigning monarch.

clue.text: Instruct comedian thus? You're having me on

definitions.meaning: a perverse order to a comic not to raise a laugh
an exclamation of disbelief at a tall story

explanation.surface: An odd instruction to a comic, followed by a suspicion of being teased.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a literal plea and a sarcastic retort meaning 'you must be joking'.

clue.text: Boss a few may find offensive

parts.note: a boss is number one, written NO 1, with I as the Roman one
some means a few

explanation.surface: A few employees may find the manager objectionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means foul-smelling or disgusting, hence offensive.

clue.text: Peculiar child… but likely to succeed?

parts.note: peculiar means odd
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A strange youngster who nonetheless seems destined for success.
explanation.walkthrough: In betting, a runner quoted at less than evens is the favourite, so is expected to win.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting slang: a horse at short prices is expected to win, hence probably going to come out on top.

clue.text: Might this indicate new place of confinement?

parts.note: read as wordplay, the centre letter of the word detention is N, the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Asks whether a fresh prison has been signposted.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer read as wordplay, 'the centre of DETENTION', gives N, which stands for 'new' in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a facility holds migrants or offenders in custody, a secure place of holding.

clue.text: Promise Labour is changing at last

indicators.note: changing at last says the final letter of the word is swapped

parts.note: sweat means hard labour, toil

explanation.surface: A pledge that the Labour Party will finally change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the party but is toil; 'changing at last' swaps the final T for R, which the clue leaves unspecified.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to promise solemnly, as on oath.

clue.text: Criminal gets gen on society's reserves

indicators.note: criminal says the letters are corrupted into a new order

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A crook obtains inside information on a society's savings.
explanation.definitionFit: Nest eggs are sums saved up for the future, i.e. reserves of money.

clue.text: Older Spaniard touring India

indicators.note: touring says one piece travels around the other

parts.note: señor is the Spanish title for a man
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An elderly man from Spain travels around India.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior describes someone of greater age or rank.

clue.text: Charlie Baker and The Witches

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an oven is something that bakes

explanation.surface: Reads like a cast list: a performer called Charlie Baker appearing in a production of The Witches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baker' looks like a surname; it is the appliance that bakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A coven is a gathering or band of witches, so it names the witches as a group.

clue.text: Bungling sees new pint knocked over

indicators.note: a drink knocked over is scattered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Clumsiness on show as someone spills a fresh pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' shuffles SEES, N and PINT together.
explanation.definitionFit: Ineptness is clumsy incompetence, the quality behind bungling a task.

clue.text: One always fuming blots Miró out

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An angry person scribbles over a painting by the Spanish artist Joan Miró.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges BLOTS MIRO; the accent is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Stromboli is an Italian volcano in near-constant eruption, so it is forever smoking.

clue.text: James running back, protecting sister

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the two clue words protect, or hold inside them, the letters wanted

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone called James jogs home while shielding his sister.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'protecting sister' as the definition, but 'protecting' is the hiding signal: James running holds ESRUN, which 'back' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a sister is a senior nurse in charge of a ward.

clue.text: Spot fashion designer briefly entering large house

indicators.note: entering says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a pile is a large stately house
CK is the short form of Calvin Klein, the fashion designer

explanation.surface: A couturier spotted walking into a mansion.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot and pickle both mean an awkward predicament, as in 'a tight spot'.

clue.text: Lagging behind, wasting time complaining

indicators.note: wasting time says the letter for time is thrown away

parts.note: trailing means lagging behind

explanation.surface: A slow worker grumbles while frittering away the hours.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to protest bitterly, so railing is complaining loudly.

clue.text: Curiously, one anti-beer is drunk

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: curiously says the letters come out in a strange arrangement

explanation.surface: The irony of a teetotal campaigner who is plastered.
explanation.definitionFit: An inebriate is a person who is intoxicated, a drunk.

clue.text: Dictionary in which one might look up 'barrister'?

definitions.meaning: a well-known British dictionary publisher's name

definitions.text: in which one might look up 'barrister'?
definitions.meaning: barristers work in sets of offices where clients visit them

explanation.surface: Where to check the meaning of a legal term.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers is a famous dictionary, and also the offices where barristers practise.

clue.text: Chinese agent's game

parts.note: the Han are China's majority people
a G-man is an FBI agent

explanation.surface: A spy from China has a game to play.
explanation.definitionFit: Hangman is a pencil-and-paper guessing game played by drawing a gallows.

clue.text: Idiot from Belfast?

parts.note: Belfast is the capital of Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI
a twit is a silly person

explanation.surface: Asks about a fool hailing from Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a twit from NI.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitwit is a foolish, stupid person, so a dimwit from anywhere qualifies.

clue.text: Look good with Her Majesty in tow?

indicators.note: in tow says the royal piece follows behind the others

parts.note: and means together with
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: An invitation to look smart while escorting the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a gander' is British slang for 'have a look'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gander is informal British slang for a quick glance or peek.

clue.text: Progressive Indian educator

parts.note: Goa is an Indian state
a head is the headteacher of a school

explanation.surface: A forward-looking teacher from the subcontinent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' looks like an adjective; it stands for the state of Goa.
explanation.definitionFit: Go-ahead describes someone enterprising and keen on new ideas.

clue.text: Torn about city contemporary

indicators.note: about says one piece goes around the other

parts.note: rent means torn
EC is the postcode district of the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone is torn about modern urban life.
explanation.definitionFit: Recent and contemporary both mean belonging to the present time.

clue.text: Way to approach half-cut sultan in Arab city

parts.note: MO, modus operandi, is a way of doing things

indicators.note: half-cut means only the first half of the word sultan is kept

explanation.surface: A road leading towards a tipsy ruler in a Middle Eastern city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for drunk; here it halves 'sultan'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mosul is a major city in northern Iraq.

clue.text: Acquiesce, needing to conceal incident

indicators.note: needing to conceal says the letters are held inside the words

explanation.surface: Someone gives in but must keep an embarrassing episode quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene is an episode or event, especially a public fuss.

clue.text: Where undergraduate might be headed, at least in part

definitions.meaning: a student is working towards a degree
the idiom meaning to some extent

explanation.surface: A student's aim, partly at least.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a student's goal of graduating; the other is an idiom for 'to some extent'.

clue.text: Government put to death four imprisoned

indicators.note: imprisoned says one piece is locked inside the other

parts.note: to execute is to put to death
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A regime kills four prisoners.
explanation.definitionFit: The executive is the branch of government that carries out the law.

clue.text: Make fun of the Speaker's letters

indicators.note: the Speaker's says the word is as someone says it, by sound

parts.note: tees are the letters T, more than one of them

explanation.surface: Mocking the correspondence of the Commons Speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker' looks like the parliamentary officer; it just signals speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To tease is to mock or poke fun at someone playfully.

clue.text: Article on diocese making you boil over

indicators.note: on says the article comes after the diocese

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a diocese leaves the reader furious.
explanation.definitionFit: To seethe is to be inwardly furious, like liquid bubbling hard.

clue.text: Disciple died in this place, guarded by soldier

indicators.note: guarded by says the soldier piece surrounds the others

parts.note: a soldier ant is a worker caste of ant
here means in this place

explanation.surface: A follower perished on this spot, watched over by a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A disciple is a follower or supporter of a teacher or cause.
